expectations.text: Cites EDPB draft Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation (consultation open until October 30, 2026), replacing the 2014 WP29 opinion once final
expectations.evidence: "EDPB Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation (adopted 7 July 2026 as version 1.0 for consultation, open until 30 October 2026). Once final, they replace WP29 Opinion 05/2014."

expectations.text: States the relative approach to identifiability per CJEU EDPS v SRB: the same dataset can be personal for one holder, anonymous for another
expectations.evidence: "CJEU, EDPS v SRB (C-413/23 P, 4 September 2025). Whether data is personal is a relative, recipient-specific assessment. Pseudonymised data may not be personal data in the hands of a recipient... The controller that holds the key still processes personal data."

expectations.text: Applies the means-reasonably-likely test and the singling-out/linkability/inference criteria
expectations.evidence: "identifiable by any means reasonably likely to be used (Recital 26)"; "the three WP29 risk criteria: singling out, linkability and inference" plus "Run the three-criteria test."

expectations.text: Distinguishes pseudonymisation (still personal data) from anonymisation
expectations.evidence: "Pseudonymised data remains personal data where additional information could re-identify people (Art. 4(5))"; "Hashing or tokenising identifiers is pseudonymisation, not anonymisation."

expectations.text: Gives practical guidance: document the re-identification risk assessment per recipient context; auxiliary data and key retention defeat anonymity claims
expectations.evidence: "Define the recipient and the context... Record the reasoning in a written anonymisation assessment"; "Include auxiliary data that is publicly or commercially available"; "an anonymity claim... may not hold for the party that holds the key"; "no sharing of keys."
